description: A re-runnable 64-point measure of AI governance health across four axes: Coverage, Control, Documentation, and Monitoring. Run it quarterly; the trend matters more than any single score.

axes.meaning: You cannot govern what you cannot see: inventory, classification, applicable regulation.
Named accountability, human oversight, failure-mode testing, vendor vetting, and the ability to stop.
Governance that cannot be proven does not exist in an audit: decisions, policies, evidence, disclosure.
Governance that is not maintained decays: scheduled monitoring, incident readiness, cadence, trend.

questions.text: We maintain an inventory of every AI system we use or build.
We have classified each AI system by risk level.
We know which regulations apply to our AI systems.
Someone is formally accountable for AI governance.
High-risk AI decisions have human oversight.
We test our models for sycophancy and failure modes.
We vet third-party AI vendors before adoption.
We can stop an AI system quickly if needed.
We document the reasoning behind key AI decisions.
We have written AI policies in place.
We can produce evidence for an auditor or regulator.
We disclose to users when they interact with AI.
We monitor deployed AI systems on a schedule.
We have an incident plan for when AI fails.
We review governance health at least quarterly.
We track AI governance maturity over time.

scoring.method: Sum the answer values across all 16 questions. Maximum 64. The weakest AXIS, not the total, tells you where to act first.

bands.recommendation: Start with the AI Governance Starter Kit and the Journey Map.
Use the Readiness Scorecard and the Stage-Gate Framework to build structure.
Adopt the Governance Operating System and a quarterly review cadence.
Pursue certification readiness and consider the Pre-Scale Governance Audit for independent assurance.

scoring.cadence: Quarterly. Log each run with its date so the trend is auditable.
